hypothesis: A resting, recovering or reply-floor-rejected melee finisher still owes its melee reply when an unwalled city spares the train from ranged strikes. It must not lend nearly free endurance to the entry budget.

simulation.profile: Four players, 60x38 Pangaea, six city-states, Online, barbarians, all victory conditions; Gran Colombia focal Domination seat versus adaptive CIVVIS, not Firaxis AI. Explicit difficulty sets player and barbarian difficulty; focal seat remains handicap-exempt as in the existing tool.
simulation.bundle: Each binary compiles the same repository live-force-on bundle; only focal spares-the-train is toggled within source. Record ledger/default and bundle hashes. Do not assume rival policy isolation without checking.
simulation.execution: Freeze baseline before the production edit; freeze candidate after the repair. Run each complete cohort exactly once. Preserve all rows, logs and exit codes, including exit 2 for no within-source action contrast. No seed replacement, clock shortening or settings changes. Do not inspect simulation outcomes until all four source-by-rung jobs terminate.
readout: Compare every OFF outcome field across sources as a reported-outcome negative control; investigate any difference.
Report all focal wins, Domination wins, conquest progress and end turns per source, rung and policy arm.
Keep the tool's within-source canonical-action equality gate; a no-contrast failure is not evidence of improvement.
Cross-source matching outcomes do not prove canonical-action identity: the existing tool does not persist those bytes or hashes.

This small simulator cohort is descriptive validation, not a Native verification, promotion screen or strength claim. Ship accounting correctness only if the regression controls and ordinary quality gates pass; unexpected simulation effects require investigation, not hidden exclusions.
